organisations, 07 organisations i.e. UPSC, SSC, LBSNAA, CAT, CBI, CVC and 
SPV Karmayogi Bharat have utilized above 77% of the funds allocated to them 
while PESB, IIPA, CIC and CBC have not been able to utilize the allocated funds 

 
69 
optimally up to 31st January, 2025. The Committee observes that ISTM and 
Lokpal have poor utilization of funds spending below 50% of the allocations and 
moreover, data shows that NRA has not spent any money out of the BE and RE 
allocation of ₹10 crore.  The Committee recommends that the Department may 
take corrective action in this regard.  
(para 2.17) 
 
4. The Committee notes that for LBSNAA Infrastructure, there is a notable 
increase in capital expenditure, with ₹82.02 crore spent till January 2025, 
demonstrating effective fund utilization. Training for All: Increased allocation in 
BE 2025-26 (₹26.16 crore) over RE 2024-25 (₹9.57 crore), but only ₹5.72 crore 
spent till January 31, 2025, indicating slow fund utilization. Domestic Funding of 
Foreign Training: Drastic reduction from ₹12 crore (BE 2024-25) to ₹0.01 crore 
(BE 2025-26), reflecting policy shift. ISTM Infrastructure: The Integrated 
Building for ISTM received ₹55.00 crore in BE 2025-26, but expenditure remains 
extremely low at ₹1.44 crore till January 2025, which indicates project execution 
delays. The Committee recommends that the Department may identify 
bottlenecks in low-spending schemes like Augmentation of Training facilities in 
ISTM and Integrated Building for ISTM and other Institute of DoPT. The 
Committee feels that there is a need for providing more funds to capacity-
building initiatives like Mission Karmayogi and Training for All. 
(para 2.22) 
 
5. The Committee recognizes the financial constraints faced by IIPA due to 
substantial increase in training programs, research projects, and academic 
activities, along with the urgent need for infrastructure renovation and 
expansion. The current allocation seems to be insufficient, potentially impacting 
the quality and efficiency of IIPA’s operations. Therefore, the Committee 
recommends that an additional Grant-in-aid be provided, based on a 
comprehensive assessment of funding requirements, to support infrastructure 
improvements, meet growing academic demands, and sustain IIPA’s capacity to 
train officers effectively.  

 
70 
(para 2.44) 
 
6. Under Revenue Head for the scheme ‘improvement of infrastructure and 
upgradation of essential facilities at LBSNAA’, an amount of ₹17 crore was 
allocated in the Budget Estimates (BE) for 2024-25, which was later revised to 
₹20.88 crore in the Revised Estimates (RE) for the same year. However, as of 
January 31, 2025, an amount of only ₹13.73 crore has been spent which is 
approximately 65.75% of the RE allocation. This expenditure falls below the 
standard set by the Ministry of Finance. The Committee, therefore, recommends 
that future budget projections be based on realistic assessment of requirements 
and the expenditure should in line with the guidelines issued by the Ministry of 
Finance.    
(para 2.49) 
 
7. The budget allocation for the Central Vigilance Commission (CVC) has 
increased marginally from ₹51.31 crore in BE 2024-25 and RE 2024-25 to ₹52.07 
crore in BE 2025-26.   While this marginal increase of ₹ 0.76 crore may 
acknowledge the Commission’s financial needs, it remains modest given 
inflation, operational expansion, and the increasing complexity of vigilance 
activities.  The Committee observes that CVC’s expenditure trend indicate 
effective financial management and is in line with with planned allocations. The 
Committee expects CVC to maintain efficiency in resource utilization while 
ensuring adequate funding for its critical vigilance functions. 
(para 2.59) 
8. The Committee notes that audit observations from previous years have 
been progressively addressed, reducing pending issues to 10 in 2023-24. While 
progress has been consistent, the complete settlement of outstanding paras 
requires timely action. The Committee emphasizes the need for timely resolution 
of pending audit paras to maintain financial transparency and compliance. It 
recommends that UPSC expedite its responses and ensure quicker settlement of 
audit observations in the future. 

 
71 
(para 2.63) 
 
PERSONNEL MANAGEMENT 
9. The existing shortage of 1316 IAS officers significantly impacts 
administrative efficiency and governance across various levels of the 
government. Given the urgency of filling these vacant posts, swift action is 
needed to enhance the recruitment process and meet the growing demands of 
public administration. The Committee, therefore, desires that the Chandramouli 
Committee’s report regarding the intake of direct recruit IAS officers may be 
studied and implemented at the earliest. 
(para 3.3) 
 
10. To ensure timely determination of vacancies in the IAS promotion quota, 
the Committee recommends that the Department of Personnel & Training may 
initiate an online tracking and submission portal for State Governments. This 
platform would allow State Governments to submit their proposals 
electronically, track the progress of their submissions, and receive automated 
reminders about deadlines. Additionally, the Department should set up a penalty 
system for delayed submissions, such as withholding consideration for promotion 
quotas from States that consistently fail to meet deadlines. This system would not 
only streamline the process but also incentivize prompt action, ensuring that the 
determination of vacancies and the subsequent promotion and selection 
processes occur without unnecessary delays. 
(para 3.4) 
 
11. The Committee recommends that the Department may establish a 
Central Monitoring and Coordination Committee to oversee and ensure timely 
and effective implementation of the data collection and recruitment processes for 
reserved category vacancies. This committee should compose of senior officers 
from DoPT, key Ministries, and a specialized unit focusing on the identification 

 
72 
and resolution of backlog vacancies.  The Committee feels by following this 
approach, reserved category vacancies may get reduced to a large extent.        
(para 3.7) 
 
12. The  Committee, therefore, recommends that a Monitoring Mechanism 
may be established to ensure timely filing of IPRs by all IAS officers. This 
mechanism should involve creation of a dedicated task force within the 
Department responsible for tracking and filing status of all officers. Additionally, 
the Committee proposes to introduce penalties or corrective actions for non-
compliance, including automatic escalation procedures for officers who fail to 
file their IPRs despite reminders. This will strengthen accountability and ensure 
timely filing, making the process more robust and ensure greater adherence to 
the requirements. 
(para 3.15) 
13. All organs of the Government of India are taken care of mainly by 
Central Secretariat Services (CSS) & Central Secretariat Stenographers’ 
Services (CSSS). They are the mainstay of Central Secretariat working.  It has 
been brought to the notice of the Committee that especially in CSS & CSSS all 
gazetted officers are rotated on the basis of sensitive and non sensitive postings 
and at sensitive places officers are replaced after tenure of 3 years.  Similarly 
Ministries have also been categorized as economic and non-economic.   The 
Committee notes that there has been a rotational policy for all officers but is not 
being implemented in toto and there are officers who are on potentially favorable 
Ministries/places for over 8-9 years, especially in economic and sensitive 
Ministries and are continuing their stay despite head of organizations been 
replaced 4-5 times. The Committee feels that this trend should be assessed. 
Longer stays at particular seats/places breeds corruption and remedial measures 
needs to be taken immediately and all transfers should be made immediately as 
per policy and no officer should stay beyond the prescribed time limit in any 
Ministry.  Secondly, the Committee wishes to point out that the Ministry of 
Finance has three department which have been categorized as economic and non 
economic, instances have come to the notice of the Committee that there are 

 
73 
instances where officers have manoeuvred their postings in such a way that their 
whole career has been in the same Ministry and hence such lacuna needs to be 
plugged without any delay. 
(para 3.16) 
RECRUITMENT INSTITUTIONS 
14.  UPSC informed the Committee that it publishes the preliminary 
examination answer key only after completing the entire selection process. This 
delays candidates' ability to challenge potential errors before advancing to the 
next stage, undermining transparency and fairness. Such a practice can 
demoralize candidates and raise concerns about the validity of the examination. 
Despite rigorous scrutiny, the possibility of errors in the answer key cannot be 
entirely ruled out. To enhance credibility, fairness, and candidate confidence, the 
Committee reiterates its recommendation contained in para 4.5 of its 126th 
report that UPSC may explore and take steps to release the answer key 
immediately after the preliminary examination and provide candidates with an 
opportunity to raise objections before proceeding further.   
(para 4.6) 
 
15.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Department should set a 
clear timeline for implementing the Baswan Committee recommendations. A 
dedicated team can be formed to prioritize key issues such as answer key 
disclosures and examination structure. Additionally, stakeholder consultations, 
including candidates and subject experts, may be conducted for effective and 
visible reforms. Regular progress updates should be published to maintain 
transparency and accountability. If any of the recommendations require policy 
changes, then they should be escalated for prompt government approval. A 
structured implementation roadmap will help modernize the UPSC examination 
process while addressing concerns about fairness, transparency, and efficiency. 
(para 4.10) 
 
16.  SSC submitted that without empirical data, it is unclear whether 
reinstating descriptive tests, either in CBT mode or traditional format, would 

 
74 
affect the recruitment cycle. A detailed assessment is necessary to evaluate 
whether descriptive evaluations enhance candidate selection without causing 
delays in the hiring process. The Committee, therefore, recommends to conduct a 
comprehensive study on the impact of descriptive tests on recruitment 
effectiveness, selection quality, and process efficiency. This study should compare 
recruitment outcomes before and after their discontinuation, assessing whether 
descriptive evaluations improve candidate competency for management posts. 
Based on the study, if reintroduction proves beneficial, a hybrid approach—
combining objective tests with limited descriptive components—could be piloted.  
(para 4.14) 
17.   The Committee appreciates that NRA has conducted a study on 
recruitment systems across Central and State agencies to identify challenges in 
implementing the Common Eligibility Test (CET). However, the findings may 
emphasize the need for a structured, transparent, and efficient examination 
framework in place at the earliest. The Committee, therefore, recommends that 
the department should expedite the finalization and implementation of 
standardized Norms, Standards, and Guidelines for CBT to ensure uniformity, 
fairness, and security in recruitment exams. A phased rollout of the Common 
Eligibility Test (CET) should be piloted across select regions before its 
nationwide implementation to assess the efficiency and address potential 
challenges. Additionally, NRA should also establish a grievance redressal 
mechanism for handling candidate concerns and for ensuring transparency. 
(para 4.19) 
18.  The Committee reiterates its concern over the significant gender gap in 
top managerial positions within CPSEs, where women constitute only 7% of the 
eligible pool and merely 7% at the Board level. Emphasizing that gender 
equality is crucial for an inclusive and accountable public administration, in line 
with the Government’s Nari Shakti policy, the Committee once again 
recommends that the Department, being the nodal agency for personnel 
management, must thoroughly examine the factors leading to the 
underrepresentation of women in leadership roles and implement concrete 
measures to eliminate barriers hindering their advancement.  

 
75 
(para 4.23) 
 
TRAINING INSTITUTIONS 
19. As per the information provided to the Committee, ISTM has been facing 
an acute shortage of staff –both faculty and non-faculty officers in the past few 
years due to a variety of reasons.   ISTM has a total sanctioned strength of 95 out 
of which 29 posts are vacant. The Committee recommends Department to take 
immediate steps to fill up the vacant posts in ISTM as shortage of staff impacts 
the effective functioning of the institution.   
(para 5.7) 
 
20. To a specific question about setting up of a study group to suggest 
reforms in the training imparted to civil servants, the Committee was informed 
that no specific Committee/ Panel/ study group to suggest reforms in the training 
imparted to civil servants at LBSNAA in the last five years have been set up by 
the Government of India. Though some changes may have been affected in the 
system of training during this period, but the time is evolving at a fast pace and 
training to civil servants requires alignment with the pace of time.  The 
Committee, therefore, recommends that the Department should establish the 
National Committee on Civil Services Training Reforms (NCCSTR) to 
modernize civil servant training. Led by a senior bureaucrat, it should include 
experts from governance, academia, industry, and international institutions. Key 
focus areas may include AI and digital governance, experiential field learning, 
ethical leadership, crisis management, and global best practices. The committee 
may submit initial recommendations in 6 months and a final report in 12 
months, with pilot implementation at LBSNAA. This will ensure future-ready, 
citizen-centric, and effective governance, enhancing the capability of civil 
servants to address evolving administrative challenges.  
(para 5.8) 
INTEGRITY, VIGILANCE, TRANSPARENCY AND SERVICE 
MATTERS 
 

 
76 
21. To reduce reliance on deputation, the Committee recommends that CBI 
develop an independent recruitment framework by allowing direct recruitment 
for core ranks like Dy.S.Ps, Inspectors and Sub-Inspectors through SSC, UPSC, 
or a dedicated CBI exam. It should also introduce lateral entry for specialists in 
cybercrime, forensics, financial fraud, and legal domains. The CBI should strive 
to establish a permanent cadre with structured career progression, this in turn 
will help CBI in ensuring long-term stability. An in-house expertise team should 
be constituted which will make it less reliable on outside experts.  Deputation 
may be retained only for select senior positions requiring diverse experience, but 
streamlining recruitment procedure and reforms will help CBI in enhancing  
operational efficiency and investigative capabilities. 
(para 6.3) 
 
22. The Committee emphasizes the need for greater transparency in 
functioning of CBI by making case statistics and the Annual Report publicly 
available on its website. The Centralized Case Management should allow public 
access to non-sensitive case details which will enhance accountability, efficiency, 
and trust in operations of CBI. The Committee believes that proactive disclosure 
of information will also empower citizens while ensuring responsible governance. 
The Committee urges CBI to implement these measures swiftly, balancing 
investigative confidentiality with the public’s right to information for a more 
transparent and responsive system.  
(para 6.6) 
 
23. The Committee notes that eight states have withdrawn general consent 
for CBI investigations limiting severely its ability to investigate corruption and 
organized crime. To address this problem, the Committee feels a separate/new 
law granting CBI wider investigative powers without state consent for cases 
affecting national security and integrity may be enacted by taking views also 
from State Governments. The law should also include safeguards to ensure 
impartiality, preventing state governments from feeling powerless. This reform 
is essential to ensure timely and unbiased investigations, prevent delays which 

 
77 
will not undermine public trust. The Committee urges action on this front which 
will strengthen the authority of CBI keeping in view the federal balance.  
(para 6.9) 
 
 
24. The Committee recommends periodic review on the effectiveness of 
Vigilance Case Monitoring System (VCMS) and based on it, improvements 
should be made. An oversight committee may be formed comprising 
representatives from the Central Vigilance Commission, CBI, vigilance 
departments, and technical experts. It should focus on reducing delays by setting 
clear timelines for case resolution, improving inter-agency coordination, and 
leveraging AI for case prioritization. This committee should also ensure user 
training and address any technical challenges faced by stakeholders. 
Additionally, it should submit bi-annual reports highlighting systemic issues and 
suggesting policy reforms to enhance efficiency and effectiveness of the vigilance 
framework.  
(para 6.12) 
 
25.  The Committee recommends that a Centralized Digital Case Repository 
(CDCR) should be established by the Central Vigilance Commission to store 
attested copies of all documents submitted to Law Enforcement Agencies 
(LEAs). Competent Authorities must be given secure access to retrieve case 
records instantly. A mandatory timeline may be in place/implemented for 
administrative authorities to submit their views on prosecution sanctions, with 
accountability measures for delays. Regular audits should be conducted to 
ensure compliance with record-keeping protocols.  Further, an inter-
departmental coordination mechanism should be introduced to expedite 
document sharing. Training programs must be conducted to ensure vigilance 
officers and administrators adhere to streamlined sanction procedures.  
(para 6.15) 

 
78 
 
26. The Committee recommends that to enhance efficiency, the Tribunal 
should institutionalize a permanent framework for Single-Member Benches in 
all pension-related and other straightforward service matters. A fixed timeline of 
90 days for case disposal should be introduced, with periodic monitoring to 
ensure adherence. Additionally, digital case management tools should be 
deployed for tracking pending senior citizen cases, prioritizing those pending for 
extended periods.  
(para 6.20) 
 
27. The Committee recommends that to ensure the timely completion of 
digitization and full implementation of Advance Case Information System 
(ACIS) in CAT, e-Courts/Smart Courts which are yet to be made fully functional 
under ACIS, needs to be made operational. The DMS should be tested 
rigorously, with feedback loops from judicial officers and litigants to ensure 
user-friendliness. Training programs should be conducted for court staff to 
enhance digital adoption. A performance review mechanism should be 
introduced to assess the impact of ACIS on case disposal rates and recommends 
further technological enhancements for efficiency.  
(para 6.25) 
 
28. The information provided indicates that the CAT Kolkata Bench is 
functioning from the CGO Complex, occupying 23,789 sq. ft., with a monthly 
license fee of ₹8,56,404. While the current arrangement meets operational needs, 
long-term financial implications should be considered. Renting space indefinitely 
results in recurring costs without asset creation. Constructing a dedicated 
building would ensure financial prudence, institutional stability, and better 
infrastructure customization. Therefore, the Committee recommends that a 
feasibility study be conducted to assess the cost-benefit of constructing a 
permanent building. If viable, necessary budgetary allocations should be made to 

 
79 
initiate the project in a phased manner, ensuring cost efficiency while 
maintaining uninterrupted functioning of the Bench.  
(para 6.27) 
29.    The Committee recommends that workforce shortages in the CIC 
should be addressed. The revival of deemed abolished ASO and MTS posts 
should be prioritized through urgent approvals.   CIC should coordinate with 
SSC for filling vacant ASO, SA, and Stenographer posts and completing the 
recruitment process within a specified timeframe. Further, a workforce planning 
framework should be introduced to anticipate future vacancies and streamline 
recruitment cycles.  
(para 6.30) 
 
30. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Department may take 
urgent steps to constitute the Inquiry and Prosecution Wings of Lokpal, 
preferably within a period of six months. The structure, staffing, and jurisdiction 
of these wings should be well defined. Recruitment of qualified personnel, 
including investigators, legal experts, and prosecutors, may be given top priority. 
Until these wings become fully operational, a dedicated coordination mechanism 
may be set up with CVC and CBI to streamline the ongoing cases. 
(para 6.33) 
31. The Committee recommends that a structured mechanism should be 
introduced to ensure timely submission of comments by public servants and 
competent authorities for timely completion of preliminary inquiries under the 
Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013. A fixed timeline may be enforced strictly for 
response submission, with automatic escalation for non-compliance. Digital 
platforms should be implemented for secure and real-time submission of 
comments to minimize procedural delays. A dedicated monitoring unit within 
the Lokpal may track compliance, issue reminders, and report persistent delays.  
(para 6.36)

INTRODUCTION 
 
 
  I, the Chairman of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on 
Personnel, Public Grievances, Law and Justice, having been authorized by the Committee to 
submit the Report on its behalf, do hereby present this One Hundred Forty Six Report on 
Demands for Grants 2025-26 pertaining to the Department of Administrative Reforms & 
Public Grievances and Department of Pension & Pensioners' Welfare (Ministry of Personnel, 
Public Grievances & Pensions). 
 
2. In accordance with the constitutional requirement under Article 113, the estimated 
expenditure of Ministries/Departments of Government of India projected under various 
Demands for Grants for the upcoming financial year need to be voted by the Parliament. 
Subsequently, the Demands for Grants of the relevant Ministries/Departments stand referred 
to concerned Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee to make a close scrutiny 
thereof under Rule 270 of Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in the Council of 
States. While making scrutiny of Demands for Grants, the Committee has made an appraisal 
of performance, programmes, schemes and policies of the Department of Administrative 
Reforms & Public Grievances and Department of Pension & Pensioners' Welfare vis-à-vis 
expenditure made out of Consolidated Fund of India. 
 
3. Demand No. 74 pertaining to the Department of Administrative Reforms & Public 
Grievances and Department of Pension & Pensioners' Welfare for the Financial Year 
2025-26 has been scrutinized by the Committee, in the Report. 
 
4. During the course of examination of the above Demands, the Committee heard the 
views of the Secretary, Department of Administrative Reforms & Public Grievances and 
Department of Pension & Pensioners' Welfare in its sitting held on 19th February, 2025.  
 
5. The Committee, while making its observations/recommendations, has mainly relied 
upon the following:-  
(i) Detailed explanatory note on DFG 2025-26 submitted by the Ministry of 
Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions; 
(ii) Detailed explanatory note on DFG 2025-26 submitted by the DARPG and 
DPPW; 
(iii) Replies of DARPG and DPPW on Questionnaire (General Issues); 
(iv) Replies of DARPG and DPPW on Questionnaire (Demand Specific); 
(v) Presentation (PPT) made by the Secretary DARPG and DPPW in the meeting of 
the Committee held on 19.02.2025; 
(vi) Detailed Demands for Grants of Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & 
Pensions.  

 6 
 
6. The Report is based on facts, figures and submissions (both oral and written) tendered 
by the Department/Institutions/Organizations to the Committee. 
 
7. The Committee considered and adopted the Report in its sitting held on the  
25th March, 2025 and presented to both Houses of Parliament on 27th March, 2025.  
8. For ease of reference and convenience, the observations and recommendations of the 
Committee have been printed in bold letters in the body of the Report.

Evolution of the Department 
1.3 In March, 1954, an Organisation and Method (O & M) Division was set up in Cabinet 
Secretariat as a follow up to one of the recommendations made by Paul H. Appleby. In 
March, 1964, a Department of Administrative Reforms was set up within the Ministry of 
Home Affairs and Organisation and Method (O & M) Division was transferred to its charge 
from the Cabinet Secretariat. On 7th February, 1973, the work relating to the Department of 
Administrative Reforms was transferred to Department of Personnel created under Cabinet 
Secretariat on 1st August, 1970 and was re-designated as Department of Personnel and 
Administrative Reforms. In April, 1977, the Department of Personnel and Administrative 
Reforms was shifted from Cabinet Secretariat to the Ministry of Home Affairs. In March 
1985, the Department of Personnel and Administrative Reforms was elevated to a full fledged 
Ministry of Personnel and Training, Administrative Reforms, Public Grievances and 
Pensions. On 10th December, 1985 Ministry of Personnel and Training, Administrative 
Reforms, Public Grievances and Pensions was re-designated as the Ministry of Personnel, 
Public Grievances and Pensions with three Departments namely, Department of Personnel 
and Training (DOPT), Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances and 
Department of Pension and Pensioners Welfare.  The Ministry was placed under the overall 
charge of the Prime Minister assisted by a Minister of State. 
About the Department 
1.4 The Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances is the nodal 
agency of the Government of India for administrative reforms as well as for redress of public 
grievances relating to the States in general and grievances pertaining to Central Government 
agencies in particular. The Department disseminates information on important activities of 
the Government relating to administrative reforms and public grievance redressal through 
publications and documentation. The Department also undertakes activities in the field of 
international exchange and cooperation to promote public service reforms. There are 8 
Divisions in the Department namely Administrative Division, Administrative Reforms (AR) 
Division, Administrative Reforms Commission (ARC) Division, Documentation And 
Dissemination (D&D) Division, e-Governance (e-Gov) Division, International Exchange & 
Cooperation (IE&C) Division,  Organization & Method (O&M) Division, Public Grievances 
(PG) Division. The Department comes under the Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances 
and Pensions and is headed by a Secretary.  
 
 
 

 11 
Functions of the Department 
1.5 As per the Government of India Allocation of Business Rules, the following subjects 
have been allocated to the Department of Administrative Reforms & Public Grievances: 
(i) Administrative Reforms, including e-governance and dissemination of best 
 practices. 
(ii) Organization and Methods. 
(iii) Policy, coordination and monitoring of issues relating to: 
(a)  Redress of public grievances in general; and 
(b)  Grievances pertaining to Central Government agencies. 
(iv) (a)  Research in public management; 
       (b)  Liaison with State Governments, professional institutions etc. in public 
  management matters. 
(v) Administration of Central Secretariat Manual of Office Procedure.  
 
 
MAJOR ACTIVITIES / INITIATIVES OF THE DEPARTMENT 
Public Grievances 
1.6 An online system for grievance redress, called the ‘Centralized Public Grievance 
Redress and Monitoring System (CPGRAMS) has evolved since 2007. The Department 
extensively uses this System to forward public grievances to the Central Government 
Ministries/Departments/Organisations as well as to the State Governments concerned. 
 1.7 Public grievance mechanism of PMO, the President’s Secretariat, the Directorate of 
Public Grievances (Cabinet Secretariat), Department of Administrative Reforms & Public 
Grievances (DARPG) and that of Department of  Pension & Pensioners’ Welfare portal are 
integrated through CPGARMS thus enabling grievances lodged to any of these entities to be 
transferred to the Central Ministries/Departments and to the State / UT Governments online 
through CPGRAMS.  
Introduction of an Appeal Mechanism/functionality in CPGRAMS 
1.8 Centralized Public Grievances Redress and Monitoring System (CPGRAMS) is one 
of the most widely used IT platforms, provides a direct access to the citizens to the 
government authorities. Citizens can file and track their grievances in CPGRAMS 24x7. All 
Ministries/ Departments of GOI and State Governments are part of this system.  The Appeal 
provision is made for redressal of dissatisfied grievances identified through a mandatory 
feedback rating to be given by the Citizen on disposal of the grievance by the Nodal 
Grievance Officers. 
  

 12 
Citizens' Charter 
1.9 A Citizens' Charter represents the commitment of the Organisation towards standard, 
quality and time frame of service delivery, grievance redress mechanism, transparency and 
accountability. Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances, in the Ministry 
of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, Government of India, in its efforts to provide 
more responsive and citizen-friendly governance coordinates the efforts to formulate and 
operationalise Citizens' Charters. Various Central Government Ministries/ Departments/ 
Organisations have brought out their Citizens' Charters. With a view to ensure effective 
implementation of Citizens' Charter, Nodal Officers have been appointed in the concerned 
Central Government Ministries/ Departments/ Organisations.   
Sevottam 
1.10 Sevottam is a generic framework for achieving excellence in public service delivery. 
It comprises of 3 modules namely, Citizen’s Charter, Grievance Redressal Mechanism and 
Capability Building for Service Delivery. As part of the Strategic plan for Capability 
Building towards implementing Sevottam Quality Management System, a Scheme for 
Strengthening of Administrative Training Institutes has been implemented during the  
12th Five Year Plan 2012-2017 in 10 States.  This Scheme was extended for a further period 
of 3 years till 31.03.2020 and for another period of a year upto 31.03.2021.  The Scheme is 
presently under review in the Department.   
e-Office - Mission Mode Project  
1.11 e-Office is one of the Mission Mode Projects approved by the Cabinet under e-
Governance Plan (NeGP). The project is aimed at significantly improving the operational 
efficiency of Central Government Ministries/Departments through improving the workflow 
mechanism and associated office procedure manuals. The Department of Administrative 
Reforms & Public Grievances is the nodal agency to monitor and facilitate implementation of 
the project. With constant monitoring and support, use of e-office has registered further 
increase with 74 Ministries have migrated to latest version of e-office 7.0. E receipt has 
grown from 32% in 2021 to 94.19% in Dec 2024. Over 80% work of Central Ministries are 
now on e-office.   
Central Secretariat Manual of Office Procedure (CSMOP)  
1.12 DARPG is responsible to bring out manual for office procedure in Central Secretariat. 
This is an important reference document provide much needed guidance to Central 
Secretariat system which saves time and efforts in figuring out processes, reduces possibility 
of mistakes and improves efficiency of employees. The Sixteenth edition of the Central 
Secretariat Manual of Office Procedure CSMOP-2022 was released on 5th August 2022. The 
new edition reflects the changes that have been brought in as a result of exercise of increasing 
efficiency in decision making and special Campaign 2.0. DARPG also brought out the first 
Hindi edition of CSMOP on 31st October 2022 to facilitate Secretariat functioning in the 
Official Language. 

 13 
Increasing efficiency in Decision Making  
 
1.13 Process re-engineering for increasing efficiency in decision making in the government 
is one of critical reforms undertaken by the Government to make the governance responsive, 
accountable and efficient. Delayering. Delegation of powers to lower formulations, 
Digitization and Desk officer system have been identified as key reforms towards increasing 
efficiency in decision making. DARPG is following up implementation and impact of these 
measures in the Central Ministries/ Department. DARPG published the Impact Analysis 
Report based on 3rd party evaluation conducted by Quality Council of India. The study 
revealed that reforms of delayering, delegation, digitization and desk officer system have led 
to defined work allocation, reduced channels of submission and timely decision making, 
embodying the principle of "Minimum Government, Maximum Governance."  
 
Special Campaign on Swachata and reducing pendency in Government offices 
  
1.14 In order to reduce pendency in the government Departments and to institutionalize 
Swachhata, the Honb'le Prime Minister Called for annual campaign for taking up these two 
objectives in mission mode. DARPG is nodal Department to curate and steer the Special 
Campaign across all institutions of the Central Government. DARPG structured the 
Campaign outline, issued the guidelines and coordinated the Campaign.  
Prime Minister’s Award for Excellence in Public Administration and Civil Services Day 
1.15 Government of India observes 21st of April every year as "Civil Services Day 
(CSD)". This is an occasion for civil servants of the country to rededicate themselves to 
citizens and renew their commitment to public service and excellence in work. The function 
is normally organized over two days. The 16th Civil Services Day was organised in Vigyan 
Bhawan, New Delhi on 20th-21st April, 2023, on the theme “VIKSIT BHARAT-
Empowering Citizens & Reaching the Last Mile”.  The Civil Services Day could not be held 
in the year 2024 due to the General Elections. The Prime Minister‘s Awards for the year 2023 
and 2024 is proposed to be conferred on the occasion of the 17th Civil Services Day on 21 
April, 2025.               
National Conference on e-Governance (Annual event)  
1.16 Department of Administrative Reforms & Public Grievances, in association with 
Ministry of Electronics & Information Technology and one of the State/UT Governments, 
has been organizing the National Conference on e-Governance (NCeG) every year since 
1997. This Conference provides a platform to the senior officers of the Government including 
IT Secretaries of State Governments, IT Managers of the Central Government, Industry, 
Experts and academia to discuss, exchange views and experiences of various e-Governance 
initiatives and road ahead.   
 
 

 14 
National e-Governance Awards 
 
1.17 To recognize and promote excellence in implementation of e-Governance initiatives, 
Department of Administrative Reforms & Public Grievances presents National Awards every 
year. The Awards are presented generally during an event of two-days, viz. the National 
Conference on e-Governance. These Awards are being given since 2003.  National e-
Governance Awards 2023 were presented during the 27th NCeG.  Total 16 awards, which 
included 09 Gold, 06 Silver Award and 01 Jury Award, were given in the 5 categories of the 
Award Scheme to Central Ministries/Departments, State/UT Governments, Districts, Local 
Bodies, Public Sector Undertakings and Academic & Research Institutions. The gold winning 
projects were given a cash award of Rs.10 lakh and the silver winning projects were given a 
cash award of Rs.5 lakh. The total award money in the 5 categories/sub-categories given was 
Rs.1.20 crores.  
 
Good Governance Webinar Series  
 
1.18 To disseminate and encourage replication of good governance practices, DARPG is 
conducting National Good Governance Webinar series on a monthly basis from April 2022. 
The themes selected for the Webinars cover various sectors like Health, Education, 
Environment, Sports- Khelo India, Innovation Category, Jal/water management, Public 
grievance redressal, Service delivery etc. Purpose is to highlight the best practices adopted by 
the award-winning initiatives for replication by other States/Districts. District Collectors, 
Secretaries in-charge of Administrative Reforms in the States/Union Territories, trainees 
from national and state level administrative training institutes and senior officials from the 
concerned line department in the States/ UTs/ Districts are invited to attend the webinars. 6 
Webinars have been held till now under the National Good Governance Webinar Series 
2024-25. The Webinar has drawn good response and will be scaled up in the next year.  
 
Good Governance Index (GGI)  
1.19 Good Governance Index (GGI) is a comprehensive and implementable framework to 
assess the state of governance across the States and UTs on identified governance parameters. 
Key objective is to create a tool which can be applied uniformly across the States/UTs to 
assess impact of various interventions made by the Central and State Governments. DARPG 
releases Good Governance Index (GGI) on biennial basis. The first GGI was released in 2019 
and the second GGI was released in 2021. The GGI 2021 evaluated performance of States/ 
UTs on 58 Indicators spread across 10 Sectors. The ten sectors covered are (1) Agriculture 
and Allied Sectors, (2) Commerce & Industries, (3) Human Resource Development, (4) 
Public Health, (5) Public Infrastructure & Utilities, (6) Economic Governance, (7) Social 
Welfare & Development, (8) Judicial & Public Security, (9) Environment, and (10) Citizen- 
Centric Governance. GGI 2025 is proposed to be taken up during the next financial year 
2025-26. 
 
  

 15 
National e-governance Service Delivery Assessment (NeSDA):  
 
1.20 The Department of Administrative Reforms & Public Grievances (DARPG) had 
constituted the National e-governance Service Delivery Assessment (NeSDA) in 2019 as part 
of its mandate to boost the e- government endeavours and drive digital government 
excellence. The study assesses States, Union Territories (UTs), and focus Central Ministries 
on the effectiveness of e-Governance service delivery. NeSDA helps the respective 
governments to improve their delivery of citizen centric services and shares best practices 
across the country for all States, UTs and Central Ministries to emulate. 
 
State Collaboration Initiatives  
1.21 DARPG Provides funds to the State Governments under the Scheme 'State 
Collaboration Initiatives' with a purpose to build collaboration with State Governments for 
improving public service delivery. The Scheme was revised in 2015-16 to include funding for 
replication of PM awarded and National e-Governance awarded initiatives.

NATIONAL CENTRE FOR GOOD GOVERNANCE (NCGG) 
1.22 National Centre for Good Governance was established as an autonomous institute 
under the aegis of the Department of Personnel and Training by upgrading the erstwhile 
National Institution of Administrative Research, Lal Bahadur Shastri National Academy of 
Administration, Mussoorie. DARPG has been made the Administrative authority for NCGG 
since 08.11.2017.  
1.23 The Centre is envisaged to be the apex think-tank that would guide the Government 
and help in implementing good Governance reforms. It seeks to be a high-level institute for 
research and capacity building to deal with the entire gamut of governance issues from the 
National to State to the local level and in sectors across the Government.  
1.24 NCGG is governed by a Governing Body, under the Chairmanship of the Cabinet 
Secretary, GoI and a Management Committee with the Secretary of the Department as the 
Chairperson.  
Objectives of NCGG 
1.25 Following are the objectives of the NCGG:  
 Conducting Capacity Building Training Programme at both National and 
International level on Public Policy & Governance; 
 To function as a national repository on information on best practices, initiatives 
and methodologies that promote Good Governance, E-Governance, innovation 
& change management within the government; 
 To initiate and participate in action research and capacity building on various 
aspects of regulatory and development administration, public policy, governance 
and public management at National/State & local levels; 
 To advise on key issues in governance and development synergy across various 
Ministries/ Departments of GoI, and State Governments; 
 To promote sharing and replication of innovative ideas and best practices in 
Governance; 
 To interact with national and international organizations, in and outside 
government, engaged in research and capacity building in the above spheres.  
 
Mandate of NCGG 
 
1.26 The mandate of the NCGG is to promote Good Governance by:  
 Carrying out Action Research/ Studies on issues relating to governance. 
 Capacity Building on Public Policy and Governance at both National and 
International level. 
 Organizing consultations, workshops, seminars/webinars & talks to promote 
improved governance. 
 Undertaking initiatives for citizen centric governance.

DEPARTMENT OF PENSION AND PENSIONERS’ WELFARE 
(DoPPW) 
About the Department 
1.27 The Department of Pension & Pensioners' Welfare was set up in 1985 as part of the 
Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions to formulate policy and coordination 
of matters relating to retirement benefits of Central Government employees. The Department 
started functioning independently with effect from April 1, 2007 with the mission to 
formulate pension policy for central government employees. The sanction process and 
implementation of the pension policy is done by the respective Central Ministry/Department. 
This department further, from time to time, simplifies the rules/guidelines and procedure to 
facilitate welfare of pensioners. All the Ministries/Departments falling under the jurisdiction 
of the Controller General of Accounts (CGA) are governed by the pension policy framed by 
this Department. However, Defence, Railways, Post and Telecom have their own processing 
and sanctioning mechanism for pension. It is noteworthy that the expenditure incurred on 
pension is directly dealt with by the Controller General of Accounts, M/O Finance for Central 
Government employees other than Defence, Railway, Post and Telecom. The Department 
also receives a large number of references from Ministries/Departments and renders advice 
on interpretation of Pension Rules which govern Central Civil service.   
Functions of the Department 
1.28 The Allocation of Business Rules broadly allocates the following areas of work to the 
Department:- 
(i) Formulation of policy and co-ordination of matters relating to retirement 
benefits to Central Government employees (Civil, Defence and Railway 
Pensioners). 
(ii) Administration of – 
(a) The Central Civil Services (Pension) Rules, 1972; the Central Civil 
Services (Commutation of Pension) Rules, 1981; the Central Civil Services 
(Extraordinary Pension) Rules, 1939; the All India Services (Death-cum-
retirement benefits) Rules, 1958, and 
(b) any other scheme relating to Central Government pensioners, entrusted to 
the Department.  
(iii) Pension structure and relief to pensioners. 
(iv) New facilities of fringe benefits to the Central Government pensioners. 
(v) Matters relating to amendment to, or relaxation of, Pension rules or any other 
rule concerning retirement benefits. 
(vi) Policy and co-ordination relating to welfare of Central Government 
Pensioners. 
 
  

 18 
Note: The action in respect of 3 above shall be subject to the concurrence of Ministry 
of Finance. Action in respect of other matters involving recurring financial 
implications by way of relaxation or liberalisation of any rule shall be subject 
to guidelines, as agreed to between the Department of Pension and 
Pensioners’ Welfare and the Ministry of Finance, Department of Expenditure. 
MAJOR ACTIVITIES / INITIATIVES OF THE DEPARTMENT 
Pensioners’ Portal 
1.29 The scheme, ‘Pensioners Portal’ was started with an objective to serve as a one stop 
information source for the pensioners of Government of India and also facilitate redressal of 
their grievances online. With the passage of time, new activities were added under the 
‘Pensioners' Portal’ which now includes CPENGRAM, Bhavishya, Anubhav and Sankalp etc. 
with an objective to create a single window system for civil pensioners.  
1.30 Pensioners’ Portal through its website provides pensioners with updated information 
on pension rules, personalized pension road map, online calculator for calculation of 
pension/family pension and redressal of Pensioners’ grievances through CPENGRAM.  
Pensioners’ Grievance Redressal Machinery (CPENGRAM) 
 
1.31 The Department, being the nodal Department for formulation of policies relating to 
pension also provides a platform for timely and structured redressal of grievances, pertaining 
to pensioners through on-line Centralised Pension Grievance Redress and Monitoring System 
(CPENGRAMS). All Ministries/Departments with their subordinate units are linked in 
CPENGRAMS with the objective to provide online resolution of the pensioners’ grievances.  
1.32 On this portal the pensioners can register their pension related grievances pertaining to 
any of the Central Government Departments/Ministries, which are then forwarded to the 
concerned Ministry/Department for redressal.  
1.33  Uniqueness of the Portal: On CPENGRAMS Portal, apart from pensioners from Civil 
Ministries/Departments, the Pensioners from Ministry of Defense, Ministry of Railways, 
Department of Posts and Department of Telecommunication can also file their grievances. For 
this, only basic information is required and log in is not required. Hence, about 64.88 lakh 
central government pensioners can file their grievances on the portal. Moreover, it is the only 
portal which is exclusively for redressal of the grievances of Central Government Pensioners. 
 
1.34 Grievances can be registered online on the portal (https://pgportal.gov.in/pension/)  
or through the Post, Email (care.dppw@nic.in) or Department’s Toll-free number:  
1800-11-1960. The last three modes are handled by Integrated Grievance Cell and Call Centre 
(IGCCC), which has been in operation since July, 2019. All such grievances of Central 
Government pensioners are registered into the CPENGRAMS and forwarded to the concerned 
Ministries or Departments promptly. 

 19 
1.35 Department of Pension and Pensioners’ Welfare operationalises Centralized Pension 
Grievances Redress and Monitoring System (CPENGRAMS), an on-line computerized 
system, developed with the objective of effective and speedy resolution of the pension related 
grievances for the Central Government Pensioners/Family Pensioners. On this system, the 
grievances are registered either directly or by DoPPW, on behalf of the complainants after 
receiving the details through e-mail, Post or Integrated Grievance Cell & Call Centre's Toll 
free number: 1800-11-1960.  
Pension Adalat 
 
1.36 These were introduced to tackle ongoing issues within the current policy, foster 
collaboration among stakeholders such as the Ministry/Department, Pay & Accounts Office, 
Central Pension Accounts Office, Bank, and Pensioner. This alternative dispute resolution 
method aims to alleviate pension-related grievances, reducing the need for legal recourse like 
courts or the Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT). The streamlined process not only 
addresses concerns more efficiently but also cuts government expenditure on legal matters, 
saving valuable time and resources.  The first Pension Adalat of the Department was held on 
September 20, 2017 in New Delhi and 11th Pension Adalat was held on August 28, 2024. 
Pension Adalat provides an additional forum for redressal of pension related grievances 
obviating the need to approach Court/ CAT.  Therefore, this would reduce time and resources 
of the Government in handling court matters. Thematic pension Adalat especially for family 
pensioners and super aged (above 80 years age) have also been extremely effective for 
redressal of grievances through pension Adalats.  
 
The ‘Bhavishya’ System 
 
1.37 To overcome the problems of delay & clerical errors in processing the pension cases, 
duplication as well as financial loss and harassment to the pensioners, the DOPPW 
introduced, on a pilot basis, a unique innovative centralized pension processing software 
called ‘Bhavishya’ for all central government Ministries/Departments.  
1.38 After a successful pilot, Bhavishya’ was made mandatory for all central civil 
Ministries and Departments w.e.f 01.01.2017. At present, 99 Ministries/ Departments, 1033 
Offices and 9168 DDOs are on Board. The ‘Bhavishya’ software was indigenously made by 
the Department of Pension & Pensioners’ Welfare and was meant to be a common platform 
for processing of pension cases by all civil Ministries/Departments of Government of India.  
Digital Empowerment of Pensioners’ - Digital Life Certificate (DLC) Campaign 3.0 
1.39 Every year in the month of November a pensioner is required to produce life 
certificate for further continuation of his pension. In the traditional mode, pensioners could 
submit life certificate by physically presenting themselves before the pension disbursing 
authority such as banks or send a certificate issued by a gazetted officer or other designated 
authorities. Due to infirmity or other ailments and old age, this manual system was a cause of 
extreme discomfort and inconvenience, as pensioners had to wait outside the bank branches 
in long queues for submission of Life certificate Keeping in view the concerns of senior 

 20 
pensioners and discomfort faced by them in the manual process, it was felt necessary to 
streamline the process to make it digital and initiate Door Step Service for submission of Life 
Certificate. 
 
1.40 In November 2014, the Aadhaar-based Jeevan Pramaan Scheme was launched to 
allow pensioners to submit life certificates online. In 2018, the DoPPW initiated the DLC 
from Home pilot program with Pensioners’ Associations, successfully creating 2,500 Digital 
Life Certificates for elderly and infirm pensioners across seven cities. 
 
1.41 To expand doorstep services for submitting life certificates, the DoPPW partnered with 
India Post Payments Bank (IPPB) in November 2020. Leveraging the network of 2,06,200 
postmen and Gramin Dak Sevaks, the DLC from Home initiative reached all corners of the 
country, especially benefiting pensioners in rural areas.. 
 
1.42 In coordination with Public Sector Banks Alliance (PSB), the DoPPW introduced 
doorstep banking services for pensioners to submit their Life Certificates by calling banking 
agents at home. To address difficulties faced by senior pensioners in submitting digital Life 
Certificates due to non-capturing of biometrics, DoPPW directed Pension Disbursing Banks 
to adopt Video-based Customer Identification Process (V-CIP), enabling a smoother process. 
Most banks have successfully implemented V-CIP for their pensioners, enhancing 
convenience and accessibility.   
 
1.43 Face Authentication Technology has been launched on 29th November, 2021 with a 
view to enhance ease of submission of Digital Life Certificate by pensioners. This technology 
allows pensioners to submit their DLC from home using an Android mobile, eliminating the 
need for external biometric devices. By capturing and submitting a live photo, pensioners' 
identities are authenticated through the UIDAI server, generating the DLC. This innovation 
has made the submission process more accessible and affordable, particularly for senior 
citizens. The technology has been widely promoted through social media platforms like 
YouTube, Facebook, Twitter, and print media, enhancing awareness and ease for pensioners.  
 
National Anubhav Awards Scheme: Recognition of Retiring Employees 
 
1.44 Anubhav is a platform for retiring government employees to share their experience of 
working with the Government. This would build up a digital documentation of legacy of 
good governance. It is envisaged that Anubhav will be nurtured as a tool for creating 
institutional memory. 99 Ministries/ Departments/ Organizations have registered on Anubhav 
Portal of this Department and more than 11,000 write-ups have been published as on 
27.01.2025.

SANKALP: Pre – retirement counseling Workshops (PRCs) 
 
1.45 Under this active initiative of ensuring pensioners’ welfare and the dignified life of 
retiring employees, the Department has been conducting Pre-Retirement Counselling 
Sessions (PRCs) for employees retiring in near future. 55 PRCs have been conducted till date 
which benefited 10762 retiring/retired personnel of various Ministries and Departments of 
Government of India. PRC covers aspects relating to timely payment of pension and 
processing formalities, CGHS benefits available to pensioners, investment options, income 
tax incentives for senior citizens/pensioners, preparation of Will and post retirement 
voluntary effort.

CHAPTER - III POLICIES, PROGRAMMES AND SCHEMES  DEPARTMENT OF ADMINISTRATIVE REFORMS & PUBLIC GRIEVANCES (DARPG) Public Grievances  Centralized Public Grievances Redress and Monitoring System (CPGRAMS)  3.0 CPGRAMS is an online system for grievance redress to facilitate citizens to lodge their grievances, for redress from anywhere and anytime (24x7) to Ministries/Departments/ Organizations/State Governments/UTs who scrutinize and take action for speedy and favorable redress of these grievances. CPGRAMS also facilitates tracking grievances through a system generated unique registration number. The grievances received manually are also digitized and uploaded on the system. The system enables Ministries/Departments to take appropriate action and upload the Action Taken Report (ATR) on the system which can be viewed by the citizens online with the help of the unique registration number.  3.1 Public grievance mechanism of PMO, the President’s Secretariat, the Directorate of Public Grievances (Cabinet Secretariat), Department of Administrative Reforms & Public Grievances (DARPG) and that of Department of  Pensioners’ portal have been duly integrated through CPGRMS thus enabling grievances lodged to any of these entities to be transferred to the Central Ministries/Departments and State Governments online through CPGRAMS.   CPGRAMS Reforms 3.2 In 2024-25 a 10-step CPGRAMS reforms process was adopted by DARPG for improving quality of disposal and reducing the time lines. The 10-step reforms include: 10 Step CPGRAMS Reform    


 28 
3.3 The 10 Step Reforms are outlined as follows:  
 
(i) Universalization of CPGRAMS 7.0 -Auto-routing of grievances to the last mile  
(ii) Technological Enhancements -Automatic flagging of urgent grievances 
leveraging AI/ML  
(iii) Language Translation –CPGRAMS Portal in 22 scheduled languages along with 
English  
(iv) Grievance Redressal Index -Ranking of Ministries / Departments on their 
Performance  
(v) Feedback Call Centre -50-seater call centre to collect feedback directly from 
every citizen whose grievance is redressed  
(vi) One Nation One Portal -Integration of State Portal and other GoI portals with 
CPGRAMS  
(vii)Inclusivity and Outreach -Empowering the remotest citizen to file grievances 
through CSC‘s  
(viii)Training and Capacity Building -Conducted by ISTM and State ATIs under 
SEVOTTAM scheme for enabling effective grievance resolution  
(ix) Monitoring Progress -Monthly reports for both the Central 
Ministries/Departments and States/UTs  
(x) Data Strategy Unit -Established at DARPG for insightful data analytics  
 
 
3.4 Impact of these Reforms: This 10-Step CPGRAMS reforms process adoption has 
resulted in a remarkable decrease in the average time of disposals of Public Grievances. In 
2023, 1.25 lac PG cases in January, 1.22 lac PG cases in February and 1.43 lakh PG cases in 
March, 1.06 PG lakh cases in April, 1.16 lakh PG cases in May, were disposed by 
Ministries/Departments. May 2023 was the 10th time in a row, since inception of CPGRAMS 
that PG case redressal has crossed 1 lac cases/month. The disposal in State PG cases on 
CPGRAMS portal has crossed 50,000 cases/month since September 2022. Average disposal 
time of Central Ministries/Departments has improved from 32 days in 2021 to 27 days in 
2022 to 18 days in 2023, to just 13 day in 2024. A significant 1,13,131 grievances were 
disposed in the month, making December the 30th month in a row where disposal crossed 1 
lakh cases in the Central Secretariat, showcasing the system's efficiency, while 58,138 
grievances remain pending, as on 31st December, 2024.  
3.5 The Committee appreciates the 10-step CPGRAMS reforms process that was 
adopted by DARPG for improving the quality of grievance disposal and reducing the 
time lines. The Committee commends the Department for faster rate of disposal of 
grievances by reducing the average disposal time from 32 days in 2021 to 16 days in 
May 2023.  To further improve the disposal rate, the Committee recommends the 
Department to integrate state portals with CPGRAMS, standardize naming 
conventions, and establish a feedback mechanism to monitor and enhance the quality of 
grievance redressal.

PROGRESS UNDER SEVOTTAM 
 
3.8  DARPG is supporting the capacity building of the grievance officers to enable them 
handle the public grievances with satisfaction of citizens. Institute for Secretariat Training 
and Management (ISTM) is the partner for providing training to the Grievance officers in 
central Ministry. ISTM has also uploaded an e-learning module on CPGRAMS on iGOT 
Karmayogi portal.  State Administrative Training Institutes (ATIs) are partners for providing 
training to the grievance officers in States. A total of Rs 1.72 crores has been released to 22 
ATIs, in the year 2024-25 till now. The Department has renewed focus on capacity building 
of the Grievance officers. Accordingly, Sevottam scheme is being reviewed and scaled up. 
The Department has also collaborated with Administrative Staff College of India (ASCI), 
Hyderabad for developing a Model Curriculum, Content, Andragogy for capacity building of 
GROs.

3.9 The Committee feels that the Department should enhance capacity-building 
initiatives for Grievance Officers (GROs) by strengthening partnerships with ISTM, 
ATIs, and ASCI. Regular training programs, both online (iGOT Karmayogi) and 
offline, may be conducted with updated content and practical case studies. Further, the 
Sevottam scheme may be reviewed and expanded for better grievance redressal. 
 
3.10 Number of feedbacks taken in the past two years and the percentage of citizens 
satisfied with the grievance redressal Grievance Redressal Index - The citizen feedback 
collected from June 2022 to December 2024 is 19.74 lac. 61% satisfaction received for the 
top 10 Ministries/Departments for the month of December 2024. The quality of grievance 
resolution improved significantly in 2024 compared to 2023, as indicated by two key metrics. 
 First, the percentage of appeals filed, relative to the number of grievances resolved, dropped 
to ~10% in 2024, signalling better initial resolutions. Second, data from the Feedback Call 
Centre shows that the percentage of satisfied complainants more than doubled, rising from 
40.74% in 2023 to 52% in 2024. This substantial increase in satisfaction rates reflects 
enhanced responsiveness and effectiveness in grievance handling, driven by ongoing reforms 
and focused follow-up by the DARPG.  
 
3.11 The Committee observes that the feedback of grievance redressal measured 
through Grievance Redressal Index, indicates positive progress with a significant rise in 
satisfaction rates and reduction in appeals, wherein the overall satisfaction rate of 52% 
in 2024 still points to considerable room for improvement. The 61% satisfaction rate for 
the top 10 Ministries/Departments is a moderate outcome, suggesting that more efforts 
are needed to achieve higher citizen satisfaction.

E-Office- Mission Mode Project 
 
3.14 e-Office is one of the Mission Mode Projects approved by the Cabinet under e-
Governance Plan (NeGP). The project is aimed at significantly improving the operational 
efficiency of Central Government Ministries/Departments through improving the workflow 
mechanism and associated office procedure manuals. The Department of Administrative 
Reforms & Public Grievances is the nodal agency to monitor and facilitate implementation of 
the project. With constant monitoring and support use of e-office has registered further 
increase with 74 Ministries have migrated to latest version of e-office 7.0. E receipt has 
grown from 32% in 2021 to 94.19% in Dec 2024. Over 80% work of Central Ministries are 
now on e-office. 
 
3.15 The following feedback/suggestions are received from the user organizations at the 
Centre/State level and implemented in the year 2024. 
(i) Records Management – Record management system for archival of physical and 
electronic files and its processes.  
(ii) 'Review Date' for parked files, helping track and manage pending tasks with timely 
reminders for follow-up. 
(iii)  Accessibility – Accessibility for visually impaired users.  
(iv) Movement of receipts across Ministries. 
(v) Integration of Bhashini for translation of voice to text and vice-versa in multi-
language support. Further, it also facilitates translation between different languages. 
(vi) Enhancement in inter-organization file movement for inter-Ministerial consultations. 
(vii) Enhancements in the audit system to enable auditors to review electronic files.  
(viii) Viewing of current status of approved drafts directly from Approver’s Sent Files 
List 
(ix) Capability to write notes in the background while referring Flags/References from 
previous notes.

NATIONAL CENTRE FOR GOOD GOVERNANCE (NCGG) 
3.19 National Centre for Good Governance was established as an autonomous institute 
under the aegis of the Department of Personnel and Training by upgrading the erstwhile 
National Institution of Administrative Research, Lal Bahadur Shashtri National Academy of 
Administration, Mussoorie. DARPG is the Administrative authority for NCGG from 
08.11.2017.  
3.20 NCGG is governed by a Governing Body, under the Chairmanship of the Cabinet 
Secretary, GoI and a Management Committee with Secretary, Department of Administrative 
Reforms and Public Grievance (DARPG) as the Chairman. 
3.21 The mandate of NCGG is to promote Good Governance by –  
a) Carrying out Action Research/Studies on issues relating to Governance. 
b) Capacity Building on Public Policy and Governance of both National and 
International level. 
c) Organizing Consultation, Workshops, seminars and talks to promote improved 
Governance.  
d) Undertaking initiatives for Citizen Centric Governance.  
3.22 Over the past two years, introductory interactive sessions on the Centralised Public 
Grievance Redressal and Monitoring System (CPGRAMS) have been conducted as part of 
training programs. These sessions focused on governance reforms, digital transformation, and 
public administration responsiveness. Specialized training on grievance redressal 
mechanisms was also provided for a comprehensive understanding.  In the post two years, 
1,921 International Civil Servants from countries like Sri Lanka, Maldives, Bangladesh, 
Kenya, Tanzania, and regional groupings such as FIPIC, IORA, LAC, BIMSTEC, SEA, and 
IOR were introduced to CPGRAMS.  Domestic Training: 224 Indian officials from 
Arunachal Pradesh (91), Jammu & Kashmir (114), and other states (19) received training 
under domestic capacity-building programs.  Impact: Participants reported improved 
understanding and expressed interest in adapting India's governance model to their regions.   
3.23 The Committee observes that the training sessions had covered only 224 Indian 
officials across select states, which is insufficient for nationwide impact.  However, it is 
also observed that States with high grievance redressal needs (e.g., Uttar Pradesh, 
Bihar, Maharashtra) were not adequately covered.  The Committee recommends that, 
to enhance the effectiveness of CPGRAMS, the Department should focus on expanding 
domestic outreach by integrating digital learning platforms and strengthening post-
training assessments.

(DoPPW) 
 
3.24 As per the Allocation of Business Rules of Govt. of India the Department of Pension 
& Pensioners' Welfare has been inter-alia allocated work pertaining to Formulation of policy 
and co-ordination of matters relating to retirement benefits to Central Government employees 
(Civil, Defence and Railway Pensioners); administration of – The Central Civil Services 
(Pension) Rules, 1972; the Central Civil Services (Commutation of Pension) Rules, 1981; the 
Central Civil Services (Extraordinary Pension) Rules, 1939; the All India Services (Death-
cum-retirement benefits) Rules, 1958, and; any other scheme relating to Central Government 
pensioners, entrusted to the Department; Pension structure and relief to pensioners; New 
facilities of fringe benefits to the Central Government pensioners; Matters relating to 
amendment to, or relaxation of, Pension rules or any other rule concerning retirement benefits 
and Policy and co-ordination relating to welfare of Central Government Pensioners. 
 
 
Pensioners' Portal   
 
3.25 DPPW is responsible for formulating policy and for coordination of matters relating to 
retirement benefits of Central Government employees with a vision to ensure active and 
dignified life for pensioners. To achieve this objective the Department, inter-alia, has 
designed and implemented the 'Pensioners' Portal'. 
 
 3.26 Pensioners’ Portal primarily aims at making the pension/retirement related 
information, services and grievance handling mechanism accessible online to the pensioners 
in addition to undertaking other activities for the welfare of pensioners. It therefore helps to 
bridge the communication gap between the pensioners and the Government. The website 
www.pensionersportal.gov.in has been created with following the features-  
 
(i) All updated orders/instructions with respect to pension/pensioners’ benefits have 
been compiled. 
(ii) Online calculator for calculation of pension, family pension, gratuity and 
commutation of pension incorporating the 7th CPC is also available on this site. 
(iii) Generation of Personalized Pension Road Map. 
(iv) PPO status enquiry for civil pensioners. 
(v) The portal has become immensely popular among pensioners.  The numbers of 
hits on the portal as on date are more than One Crore.

that MOD requires targeted intervention rather than general reforms.  The Committee, 
therefore, recommends the Department to establish a specialized grievance cell with 
representatives from MOD, PCDA, and Ex-Servicemen Welfare to identify key 
bottlenecks and expedite timely resolution of grievances. 
  

 38 
3.37 There has been overall 42% increase in the receipts of the pensioners’ grievances in 
2024 over 2023, which is mainly contributed by Ministry of Defense with the increase in 
75% of the grievances. Active and regular interaction with MOD has ensured the pace of 
redressal of the grievances is maintained.  
 
3.38 The details of average time taken for the redressal of grievances lodged by Super 
senior citizens aged 80 years and above during the last three years are depicted in following 
table:

II. PENSION ADALATS 
3.39 This Department had started the unique experiment of holding Pension Adalats to 
resolve chronic grievances of Central Govt. Pensioners, falling within the four walls of extant 
policy. These Adalats, as the term might sound, do not have any judicial or quasi-judicial 
powers but have proved a highly successful mode of grievance resolution. All the stake-
holders of a particular grievance are invited on a single table viz. the concerned 
Ministry/Department, the Pay & Accounts Officer of the concerned Department, the CPAO 
(Central Pension Accounts Officer, Ministry of Finance), the concerned Bank and the 
Pensioner or his/her representative and they resolve the case across the table. 
3.40 Under this system, all stakeholders for a particular grievance - viz. concerned 
Ministry/Department,  Pay & Accounts Office, Central Pension Accounts Office, the 
concerned Bank and the Pensioner or his/her representative - are invited on a common 
platform. The issue is discussed among all the stakeholders and resolved across the table. In 
cases where additional information is required, a fixed time is given to decide the matter and 
the unresolved grievances are monitored by DoPPW on regular basis. On a given date, 
DoPPW arranges Pension adalat for chronic grievances in the CPENGRAMS, covering 
various Ministries/Departments. Other Ministries / Departments are advised to hold pension 
adalats simultaneously for their pensioners, in different parts of the country. Till date Eleven 
Pension Adalats have been conducted by DoP&PW and out of  25,224  cases taken up in the 
Pension Adalats, 18,005 grievances were resolved (71.38%) by the different 
Ministries/Departments/ Organisation which participated in this initiative.  

 39

3.42 The Committee appreciates the Department for holding Pension Adalats every 
year since 2017. The Committee is of the view that, while the Nationwide Pension 
Adalats have played a crucial role in grievance redressal, the resolution rate of 71.38% 
indicates that nearly 29% of cases remain unresolved, which raises concerns about 
efficiency. The Committee therefore, desires that efforts may be made to address the 
unresolved cases by constantly pursuing them with the concerned Departments. 
III. SANKALP 
3.43 A number of pensioners feels the loss of a daily routine as well as of feeling of not 
being wanted.  Keeping these factors in mind a new initiative of the Department, christened 
as Sankalp, has been taken up to prepare them for post-retirement life and channelize 
experiences and skill of retired Government servants towards meaningful interventions in 
Society.  
3.44 Under this active initiative of ensuring pensioners’ welfare and the dignified life of 
retiring employees, the Department has been conducting Pre-Retirement Counselling 
Sessions (PRCs) for employees retiring in near future. 55 PRCs have been conducted till date 
which benefited 10762 retiring/retired personnel of various Ministries and Departments of 
Government of India. PRC covers aspects relating to timely payment of pension and 
processing formalities, CGHS benefits available to pensioners, investment options, income 
tax incentives for senior citizens/pensioners, preparation of Will and post retirement 
voluntary effort.  
  

 40 
IV. ANUBHAV  
3.45 Anubhav is a platform for retiring government employees to share their experience of 
working with the Government. This would build up a digital documentation of legacy of 
good governance. It is envisaged that Anubhav will be nurtured as a tool for creating 
institutional memory. 99 Ministries/ Departments/ Organizations have registered on Anubhav 
Portal of this Department and more than 11,000 write-ups have been published as on 
27.01.2025. 
 
3.46 An annual Anubhav Awards scheme was introduced in 2015 to incentivise and 
encourage the participation. 59 Anubhav awards and 19 Jury certificates have been conferred 
in seven Ceremonies held so far.  
V. BHAVISHYA 
3.47 Implementation of Bhavishya in all Ministries/Departments; governed by 
CCS(Pension) Rules, 1972/CCS(Pension) Rules, 2021-DOPPW introduced and fine-tuned 
an online pension processing software called ‘Bhavishya’ for all central government Civil 
Ministries/Departments. This software brought on a common platform, all the stakeholders 
who were till date decentralized. The involved integration of PFMS (Public Finance 
Management System) of Controller General of Accounts and PARAS (Pension 
Authorization, Retrieval and Accounting System) of Central Pension Accounts Office under 
the Ministry of Finance. The system laid down a common methodology incorporating all the 
rules and regulations of CCS Pension Rules, 1972/ CCS Pension Rules, 2021 and automatic 
calculation of pension. This system does automatic pension processing of dues and therefore 
eliminates manual intervention ensuring transparency in the system. The system on its own 
keeps throwing up alerts to the pensioner as well as to the stakeholder for meeting the 
deadlines prescribed for various stages of Pension processing. At present, 99 
Ministries/Departments, 1033 Offices and 9168 DDOs are on Board and 268290 e-PPOs 
have been issued till 24.01.2025.  
 
3.48 New Pension Application Form and integration with e-HRMS:- This form will be 
available in Bhavishya/e-HRMS to all the Central Government Employees who are going to 
retire in December 2024 and onwards. This New form and its integration with Bhavishya/e-
HRMS was launched on 30th August 2024, at National Media Center, New Delhi, under 
auspicious presence of Hon’ble Shri Dr Jitendra Singh Hon’ble MoS (PP).  This new form is 
integrated with Bhavishya/e-HRMS. The retiring officials, who are on e-HRMS, are filling 
Form 6-A through e-HRMS (only Superannuation cases) and the retiring officials, who are 
not on e-HRMS, are filling Form 6-A in Bhavishya w.e.f 16.10.2024. As on 29.01.2025, 
more than 8890 retiring officials have submitted new Form 6-A in Bhavishya whereas one 
retiring official has successfully submitted Form 6-A in e-HRMS.  
 
  

 41 
3.49  Integration with CGHS: Department of Pension & Pensioners’ Welfare (DoPPW) is 
dedicated in improving the Ease of Living for pensioners through continuous enhancements 
in Pension Rules and Procedures. Department of Health & Family Welfare (DoHFW) 
proposed for integration of CGHS Card application with Bhavishya Portal for the retiring 
central government employees. DoPPW immediately agreed to the proposal of DoHFW.This 
would entail that all retiring government employees would have an ensured medical cover 
from the very first day of retirement.  
 
3.50 Integration with Banks: 2 new banks integrated with Bhavishya viz Central Bank of 
India and Union Bank of India.This integration serves as a single stop for all facilitation of 
documentation like Income Tax certificate, Pension Slip, Due and drawn statements, DLC 
status for the pensioner.  
3.51 The Committee commends the overall performance of the Department of Pension and 
Pensioners Welfare and hopes that it will continue with its good work to bring about 'ease of 
living' for pensioners, especially for super senior citizens and family pensioners.  
3.52 Main achievements/activities of Department of Pension and Pensioners’ Welfare - 
100 days Plan and Achievements - 2024-25:- 
(i) The Department of Pension & Pensioners’ Welfare (DoPPW) has implemented 
several initiatives in 2024 aimed at enhancing the welfare of pensioners, 
streamlining grievance redressal, and promoting digitization in pension processes. 
(ii) Month long campaign for effective redressal of family pensioners grievances 
redressed 1737 family pensioners grievances. 
(iii) 54th Pre-Retirement Counselling Workshop was held at Jammu under the 
chairmanship of Minister of State for Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions 
to facilitate officials who are about to retire in the superannuation process. 
(iv) Instructions for enhancement of maximum limit of retirement gratuity and death 
gratuity for central government employees from Rs.20 lac to Rs. 25 lac on 
reaching the Dearness Allowance rates to 50 percent. 
(v) 5 Anubhav Awards and 7 Jury Certificates were conferred under Anubhav 
Awards Scheme 2024.  
 
SOME GENERAL RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS:- 
3.53 Sankalp – A number of pensioners feels the loss of a daily routine as well as of 
feeling if not being wanted.  To alleviate this condition and keep them busy, physically, 
mentally and to remain relevant in society it will be a great help that the Department 
opens CSOI branches in NCR to start with immediately and till such a time this facility 
comes up the Department may take up with Haryana and UP Govt. to allow 
membership of their existing clubs to the pensioners who do not hold CSOI membership 
as on date.  This facility will go a long way in improving the quality of life to remain 
physically and mentally agile. 

 42 
3.54 CGHS – A large number of Pensioners are availing CGHS facilities, as a welfare 
measure the pensioners may be allowed to avail private hospitals facilities without the 
necessity of referral slip from the dispensaries.  The Committee feels this will reduce a 
lot of mental and physical pressure on pensioners and the matter may be taken up with 
the Ministry of Health & Family Welfare to issue necessary instructions in this regard. 
3.55 Pension – The Committee observes that many a times the disbursing banks take 
away money unilaterally in the name of over disbursal, without even informing the 
pensioners and that too in one go.  Since pension is meant for sustenance such a money 
lender behaviour or a coercive measure of taking funds on its own by the bank goes to 
show a complete disrespect to the system.  The Committee feels that the banks should be 
sensitized about it and this sort of exercise should be stopped immediately. 
 
3.56 The Committee appreciates the Department of Pension and Pensioners Welfare 
for its overall performance and hopes that it will continue good work to bring about 
'ease of living' for pensioners, especially for super senior citizens and family pensioners.

DEPARTMENT OF ADMINISTRATIVE REFORMS AND PUBLIC GRIEVANCES 
(DARPG)
